## Why This Is Asked

Tests for idempotency are crucial in high-concurrency flows to prevent duplicate orders. This question probes reliability, concurrency handling, tenant isolation, and TTL-based cleanup.

## Key Concepts

- Idempotency keys and deduplication
- Concurrency and race conditions
- Multi-tenant isolation and header-based scoping
- TTL-based cleanup and data retention
- Error handling paths and resilience

## Code Example

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/orders \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: A' \
  -H 'X-Tenant-ID: t1' \
  -d '{"item":"widget","qty":1}'
```

```javascript
// Pseudo test sketch
const r1 = post('/orders', payload, { idKey: 'A', tenant: 't1' })
const r2 = post('/orders', payload, { idKey: 'A', tenant: 't1' })
assert(r1.orderId === r2.orderId)
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you detect flaky idempotency tests in CI?
- How would you extend tests for eventual consistency or cross-region deployments?

## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates understanding of idempotent API design, asynchronous workflows, and comprehensive testing strategies in distributed systems.

## Key Concepts
- Idempotency keys prevent duplicate operations
- Asynchronous job processing and status polling
- Input validation and error response design
- Concurrent request handling and race conditions
- Test isolation and data management
- Tooling selection for different testing phases

## Code Example
```javascript
// Jest test example
const payload = {cart: [{id: 'p1', qty: 2}], currency: 'USD'}
const headers = {'Idempotency-Key': 'abc-123'}

const response1 = await request(app)
  .post('/checkout')
  .set(headers)
  .send(payload)
  .expect(202)

const response2 = await request(app)
  .post('/checkout')
  .set(headers)
  .send(payload)
  .expect(200)

expect(response1.body.jobId).toBe(response2.body.jobId)
```

## Code Example

function sha256(data){ return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex'); }
